Vendored mojito-sys S6.2 socket substrate —
mojito_async/vendor/mojito-sys/mjs_socket.c

Source repository: github.com/mojito-async/mojito-sys
Source tree:       native/posix/mjs_socket.c
Source commit:      a26e9a3550511738252174278af0794f6cbfd104 (main)
Vendored on:        2026-08-28 (A7.3/A7.4 productionization, issues #77/#78)

Layers on the SAME include/mojito_sys.h the A7.1/A7.2 reactor lane already
vendored whole (mojito_async/vendor/mojito-sys/VENDORED_AT_S6.txt) — the
s6-socket header block was diffed byte-identical between that lane's
vendored commit and this one's before vendoring (both frozen since the
mojito-sys S6.2 milestone), so no second header copy is introduced here.

mojito_async/vendor/mojito_sys_io/externs.mojo's own header notes it was
"TRIMMED to the s6-poller/s6-epoll/s6-ioring sections only" by the #75/#76
lane, deliberately leaving the s6-socket (mjs_socket_*) bindings for this
lane to add — done in this commit (the s6-socket externs block + probe_*
shims, inserted ahead of the s6-poller section, vendored from the SAME
mojito-sys commit as mjs_socket.c above).

DEVIATION FROM FROZEN ABI (issues #77/#78, RECORDED): mjs_socket.c gains
TWO entry points not in the upstream frozen s6-socket block, appended
after mjs_socket_close with their own header comment:
  mjs_socket_set_reuseaddr(fd, enabled) — SO_REUSEADDR, for
    bind_and_listen's "rebind immediately after restart" deliverable
    (issue #78).
  mjs_socket_connect_error(fd, *out_err) — getsockopt(SO_ERROR), the only
    way to decode a pending non-blocking connect()'s eventual outcome
    once write-readiness fires (issue #77 plan step 3); the frozen ABI
    has no other way to express this. Return contract matches every
    other entry point (0/-errno); *out_err separately carries the
    connect() outcome (0 established, positive errno on failure).
These are NOT upstreamed to github.com/mojito-async/mojito-sys; they are
local additions layered on the vendored copy, matching the deviation
pattern already recorded in vendor/mojito-sys/VENDORED_AT.txt (M:N ctx
rework). Matching @extern declarations live at the end of
vendor/mojito_sys_io/externs.mojo; see vendor/mojito_sys_io/socket.mojo's
module docblock for the Mojo-side wrapper methods
(NativeSocket.set_reuseaddr/connect_error).

The Makefile's `mojito_async/vendor/mojito-sys/*.c` wildcard picks this up
automatically; no Makefile edit needed.

UPDATE (issue #182): mjs_socket.c gained TWO more local-only entry points,
appended right after mjs_socket_connect_error with their own header
comment:
  mjs_socket_set_sndbuf(fd, bytes) — setsockopt(SO_SNDBUF).
  mjs_socket_set_rcvbuf(fd, bytes) — setsockopt(SO_RCVBUF).
Both exist so a test can shrink a socket's kernel buffer to a known-small,
deterministic size instead of depending on the platform's auto-tuned
default — t44_tcp_read_write_aot scenario B's 512KB write_all needs at
least one real EAGAIN/EWOULDBLOCK, and the platform default for either
buffer was sometimes large enough on its own to swallow the whole payload
in one non-blocking burst (confirmed flaky on this host: 5/20 standalone
runs of the unmodified binary). Same return contract, same "not
upstreamed" status as the SO_REUSEADDR/SO_ERROR pair above. Matching
@extern declarations + probe_* shims live at the end of
vendor/mojito_sys_io/externs.mojo (own "issue #182 deviation externs"
block); Mojo-side wrappers are NativeSocket.set_send_buffer_size/
set_recv_buffer_size (vendor/mojito_sys_io/socket.mojo) plus a
TcpStream.set_send_buffer_size passthrough (net/tcp_stream.mojo) since
TcpStream does not otherwise expose its underlying NativeSocket — no
TcpStream-level recv-buffer passthrough (adversarial review, PR #188):
t44 scenario B's receive side is a raw NativeSocket, not a TcpStream, so
nothing calls one; add it once a real caller does.
VENDORED_EXCEPTIONS.tsv's mjs_socket.c row hash was updated to match.
